CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

zutempo implements the Temporal date and time model of ECMA-262 in R: Instant, ZonedDateTime, PlainDateTime, PlainDate, PlainTime, PlainYearMonth, PlainMonthDay, Duration and Now, in the ISO 8601 calendar, with IANA time zones read from the same database base R uses. The arithmetic is a transliteration of the specification’s abstract operations into C over the specification’s full ranges, so a result in R matches the result in a browser or in Node. It has no hard runtime dependency: zufast is LinkingTo only (header-only C, needed at build time). It does not do non-ISO calendars, locale formatting, custom time zones, strftime, or arithmetic operators in 0.1.0.

The specification is .agents/design.md and the plan is .agents/roadmap.md. They outrank this file: CLAUDE.md orients, the design decides, the roadmap says what each stage builds and when it is done.

Current state

Verified 2026-10-15: package identity only (stage 0). src/ holds the registration entry point and nothing else; no R function exists yet. The engine, the types and the time zone reader are not implemented. See the roadmap’s stage table for what is done.

Stage tracking

Progress toward the next version is tracked as GitHub sub-issues, so the parent issue shows a progress bar such as “6 of 14”.

  • One parent issue per target version, titled with the bare version: v0.1.0 (#2).
  • One sub-issue per roadmap stage, titled as the roadmap titles it, for example Stage 2 — PlainDate, PlainTime and PlainDateTime, and linking to that section. The roadmap has fourteen stages, 0 to 13.
  • Every tracking issue carries the stage label, so it can be told apart from bug and feature issues and left out of open-issue counts.
  • Close a stage by merging its pull request. Put Closes #<n> in the body of the stage’s pull request. Never close a stage whose exit criteria are not met; record a deviation in the roadmap first.
  • The roadmap stays authoritative. The issues record which stages are done, not what a stage requires. Adding, removing or renaming a stage means editing the roadmap and the sub-issues in the same change.
  • Close the parent issue when CRAN accepts the version and it is tagged.

Versioning

The package develops at 0.0.0.9000 and targets 0.1.0 for its first CRAN release. Set Version: 0.1.0 and the matching NEWS.md heading when the package enters Pre-flight. Bump to 0.1.0.9000 only after CRAN accepts it, never before.

zutempo depends on zufast through LinkingTo and develops against its default branch (Remotes: pedrobtz/zufast) until zufast 0.1.1 is on CRAN; zutempo is not submitted before then (roadmap, open question 1). Nothing depends on zutempo yet. The C table for other packages (design §7) comes after 0.1.0.

Commands

Run from the package root.

Rscript -e 'devtools::load_all()'                # compile src/ and load
Rscript -e 'devtools::document()'                # roxygen -> NAMESPACE, man/
Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'                    # full testthat suite
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "<name>")'   # one test file
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE)'      # order independence
Rscript -e 'devtools::check()'                   # R CMD check
air format .                                     # format R sources

The default loop is document(), test(), check(). Before the first load_all(), install the development zufast: Rscript -e 'pak::pak("pedrobtz/zufast")'.

Architecture

Design §4 is the reference. The layers, top down:

  • R/: argument and option normalisation, recycling, class and attribute handling, vctrs and pillar methods registered lazily.
  • src/ztp_r_*.c: the glue. R vectors in, column loops, NA handling, conditions raised with the 1-based index of the failing element.
  • src/ztp_*.c: the engine. The specification’s abstract operations over plain C structs, one C function per operation where practical, each commented with the section it implements. No SEXP, no R calls, no allocation in loops. Calendar algorithms and 128-bit intermediates come from zufast’s headers.
  • src/ztp_tz*.c: the zone cache. TZif reader, POSIX TZ footer rules, link table, identifier index.
  • src/init.c: the only exported symbol, R_init_zutempo.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • The engine never calls R. Errors are status codes plus a message in a per-call buffer; the glue turns them into conditions. This is what lets the same engine serve C callers after 0.1.0. An Rf_error() or an allocation inside ztp_*.c breaks that.
  • Values are stored exactly in R’s own vector types (design §4.1). No bit reinterpretation, no 64-bit integers smuggled in doubles. 128-bit integers exist only inside C.
  • Nanoseconds are normalised to [0, 1e9) with the floor convention, so lexicographic order on (Re, Im) of a complex value is chronological order.
  • Every TZif count and offset is bounds-checked against the file size before use. The reader is a fuzz target.
  • A slim TZif file needs the POSIX footer. R’s own database is slim; macOS’s is fat, which hides a footer bug on the developer’s machine (design §0).
  • Duration fields are doubles because Temporal’s are. Field-to-normalised conversion is a sum of products in 128 bits, never a double computation.
  • The pinned specification moves only on purpose. inst/spec/PINS records the tc39/proposal-temporal and test262 commits; changing either needs its own NEWS.md entry.
  • The suite must build and pass with ZUF_NO_INT128 as well as with __int128. CI runs both.

Testing conventions

  • Self-sufficient. Every test builds its own inputs inside the test_that() block. No file-scope objects.
  • Self-contained. Global state goes through withr::local_*(), randomised input through withr::local_seed(). Tests write only under tempdir().
  • Assert on condition classes, never message text. Use expect_error(..., class = "zutempo_<kind>_error"). Wording belongs in snapshot tests.
  • Order independence. devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE) is part of the definition of done.
  • Borrow a conformance suite before writing one. The oracle is temporal-polyfill under Node (tools/temporal-oracle/, from stage 1), checked against Node 26’s native Temporal; test262’s result assertions are translated in stage 11. Zone cases run against committed TZif fixtures from a pinned tzdata release, not the machine’s database.
  • Tests that need the machine’s database skip when it is missing.
  • Helpers live in tests/testthat/helper-*.R. helper-oracle.R runs every case in an oracle JSON file (from stage 1).
  • Keep the suite inside the CRAN time budget. Not yet measured.

Definition of done

devtools::document() and devtools::check() clean, meaning 0 errors, 0 warnings and 0 notes. The one allowed note is “New submission” before the first release. devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE) green. gctorture(TRUE) clean when C changed. CI green on every leg. A user-facing change also needs a test, roxygen documentation and a NEWS.md entry.

Releasing to CRAN

  • CI is the pre-submission check. The pedrobtz/r-actions R CMD check runs --as-cran on the CRAN-like runners and containers, and it replaces win-builder, the macOS builder and R-hub. None of them is a release step, and cran-comments.md lists the CI legs as its test environments.
  • Entering Pre-flight. The roadmap’s feature stages are done, the version is set as in Versioning, NEWS.md and cran-comments.md are written, and CI is green. Only submission work remains.
  • Before submitting, run the pkg-cran-review skill and resolve every finding.
  • The pretest is automated and does not read cran-comments.md. A NOTE that is explained but not fixed gets the upload archived. Fix the NOTE instead of justifying it.
  • After acceptance, tag v0.1.0, publish the GitHub release, bump to 0.1.0.9000, and close the version’s parent issue.

Editing rules

  • roxygen comments are the source. Never edit man/ or NAMESPACE by hand.
  • Edit README.Rmd, not the generated README.md (from stage 12).
  • Keep prose simple and short. One idea per sentence. British spelling.
  • Wrap roxygen text at 80 characters and run air format . on R sources.
  • Use lower_snake_case. R names follow design §5: constructors named after the type, temporal_ for methods, accessors named after the property, now_ for Temporal.Now, zutempo_ for package helpers. Internal native symbols are prefixed ztp_; the public C prefix is zutempo_.
  • Keep hard runtime dependencies at zero. zufast is LinkingTo only.
  • Export and document public functions. Do not create roxygen topics for internal ones.

Continuous integration

Workflows come from pedrobtz/r-actions. Call those reusable workflows instead of writing bespoke ones, and pin a released tag rather than main. Pin a workflow that holds a write token, such as coverage.yml, to a commit, with the tag in a comment. The R-CMD-check workflow must call r-cmd-check.yml, because a hand-rolled one does not count as the pre-submission check.

This package calls:

  • R-CMD-check.yaml: r-cmd-check.yml@v1, quick on pull requests, full on main or with the full-ci label.
  • native-checks.yml: valgrind.yml, lto.yml, gctorture.yml, rchk.yml (with github-packages: pedrobtz/zufast, since the rchk image ignores Remotes:), analyzers.yml and cran-special.yml, with the same profile expression. sanitizers.yml (with ASan) joins in stage 1, once there is C for it to instrument (pedrobtz/r-actions#68).
  • coverage.yaml: coverage.yml pinned to a commit. The badge is committed to gh-pages because main takes no direct pushes.
  • pkgdown.yaml: the r-lib site build, deploying to gh-pages with force: false so it does not overwrite the badge.

Small edits get a small run. The shared workflows look at the files a pull request changes, compared with its merge base:

  • Markdown only, such as README.md, NEWS.md or cran-comments.md, skips every check. Only coverage and the pkgdown site run.
  • DESCRIPTION or README.Rmd as well, and nothing else, adds one R CMD check on Ubuntu R-release.
  • Any other file runs everything.

So put a README or DESCRIPTION touch-up in its own pull request. Once a pull request changes code, every later push to it runs in full.

Commits and pull requests

Short, imperative, sentence-case commit subjects, optionally scoped. Keep each commit focused and do not sweep in unrelated files. A pull request explains the user-visible outcome and the rationale, links related issues, lists the checks that were run and the tests that were skipped, and flags platform-sensitive changes. Performance claims need evidence.

Never commit or push to the default branch. Work on a branch, open a pull request, and merge it only when every check is green. A stage’s pull request closes its sub-issue.

When you find a defect, in this package or in an upstream tool, open an issue for it rather than only working around it.
